newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-David Jones sees no bumper Christmas.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-David Jones sees no bumper Christmas.

text.p: Australian upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd said on Thursday it was not counting on a bumper Christmas sales season and predicted extremely tough trading conditions until then.
"I don't detect any movement in the retail climate," David Jones chief executive Chris Tideman told reporters here.
"I think it's going to be extremely tough through to Christmas. Having said that, it's always amazing how people do dig deep in the festive season,
"Christmases generally do not turn out to be too disappointing, but is it going to be a rip-roaring bumper one? I don't think so."

Earlier, in a speech to a Property Council of Australia luncheon, Tideman said the department store chain would continue to try to preserve profit margins during the retail downturn by focusing on its high-margin clothing merchandise.
He described this strategy as "something we must do and will do" and said David Jones' strategy was to position itself as Australia's pre-eminent upmarket retailer when the upturn came.
"That's a long-term strategy we have in place and we are going to proceed with it irrespective of the short-term market conditions we are facing," Tideman said.

Outlining the company's store expansion and refurbishment programme, Tideman said four new stores were on the drawing board, including the announcement earlier on Thursday of a new store to be built in Melbourne's fast-growing outer east.
The new Melbourne store, to be built in suburban Fountain Gate, will cost around A$20 million, including initial stock, he said.
Tideman also announced that he would soon lead an investment roadshow for David Jones to explain the recently-listed stock to institutional investors in the United States and Europe.

But he said David Jones was not planning to raise capital on the market and said capital expenditure, running at about A$55 million in the current 1996/97 year (July/June), would be funded internally.
"We are planning our capital expenditure going forward out of cash flow," Tideman said.
